readAfter: adjudication.json was written, and score-skill.json, analysis.json and the cross-route analysis were computed. The reader is the corpus author, who has seen the scores. Reading can add observations; it changes no as-run number.
procedure: As v3-run/PREREGISTRATION.md fixes it: (1) every evidence-gap twin any arm judged GO, (2) every defect twin without NO_GO, (3) every sound plan with NO_GO, (4) a sample of up to ten sound plans the skill-style arm judged GO_WITH_CHANGES and the sentence arm judged GO, (5) a sample of up to ten correct evidence-gap twins from each arm. Reports were read through the saved report text (truncated at 750 to 2,600 characters for the long ones, with the machine summary or verdict line); the packets were read for (1) and (4).

4_skillHedgedAndSentenceGoSoundPlans.rule: one unit per family that has any such unit, lowest case id, trial 1 where available (10 families: flag_default, backup_window, cert_rotation, rollback_window, storage_access, credential_logging, unique_constraint, retry_idempotent, payload_limit, payment_idempotency_key)

skill.rule: one per family with a correct twin (7 families), then a second case from capacity_headroom, payload_limit and rollback_window

overclaimedEvidenceGapTwins.rule: three families per arm, first NO_GO observation each (skill: upgrade_compat, rate_limit_quota, retry_idempotent; defined: payload_limit, rollback_window, unique_constraint; defined-go: retry_idempotent, rollback_window, payload_limit)

findings.evidenceGapTwinJudgedGo: defined-go trial 2, storage_access A (Q-24fc1f). The report states 'Nothing stated in the plan makes it fail', names the unestablished fact as the 'Main risk' (nobody has tried writing to the bucket with svc-export's credentials or checked its permissions), spells out that a failure costs the day's release, recommends a write test, a reader-access check, an alert and a fallback, and then calls these 'optional, but cheap and worth doing' and 'steps [that] make the plan more robust', ending VERDICT: GO. This is the v2 mechanism exactly: the gap is named and then classed as an optional robustness step under the added sentence. It is 1 of 32 observations here; the same case under the same arm in trial 1 was GO_WITH_CHANGES.
findings.soundPlansHedgedBySkillStyle: All ten reports found no blocker and answered the fixed question with No; the hedge came from RISK or NOTE findings, mostly marked UNVERIFIED or CANNOT_CHECK. Most raise something the plan does not say rather than something it contradicts: an unevidenced 'single code path' claim (unique_constraint), a 1 KB write test against a 30 GB write (storage_access), a rescan of the unbounded notes field in later months (payload_limit), a redaction denylist and the log store's exposure (credential_logging), when the outage clock starts and whether a column drop loses data (rollback_window), a missed weekly backup against the retention margin (backup_window), no gate before the old root is removed (cert_rotation), a schema change outside the flag and a mixed state during a flip (flag_default), whether staging overlapped sends (retry_idempotent), and whether declined charges count as seen keys (payment_idempotency_key). Several are defensible reads of residual gaps (the Gemini reviewer hedged one plan each in the unique_constraint and storage_access families too); none invents evidence or promotes a gap to a blocker. The pattern is thoroughness: this reviewer lists what the plan does not prove, and the skill-style prompt invites it.
findings.correctEvidenceGapTwins: All 26 reports read (skill 10, defined 6, defined-go 10) named the unestablished fact in their own words, tied it to the plan's stated requirement and the cost of being wrong, said explicitly that it is a risk and not a proven defect (the skill-style reports quote the review contract's rule), and recommended a measurement, a confirmation or a check. None dismissed the gap and none invented evidence. The verdict-only arms' correct reports are long reviews headed 'The main risk' or 'The gap'; the skill-style reports end in a MACHINE SUMMARY with a RISK finding on the gap line (UNVERIFIED in 9 of the 10, CANNOT_CHECK once).
findings.overclaimedEvidenceGapTwins: The nine NO_GO reports read show the failure mode of this corpus on the Claude route: the reviewer names the gap correctly and then rules it a blocker. The skill-style reports say 'I am not claiming the callers will break; that would treat missing evidence as a proven defect' and then 'the blocker is narrower: the plan ships against a requirement it admits is unverified', writing BLOCKER | VERIFIED on the line that states the gap (upgrade_compat) or BLOCKER | UNVERIFIED (retry_idempotent: 'I rate this a blocker rather than a risk'). The verdict-only reports go further and add failure mechanisms the plan text does not state (a DROP COLUMN that rewrites a 400 GB table, lock queues, 7.3 traffic breaking during the drop, a larger payload than the stated scan) and conclude the plan 'should not ship tonight'. In every case the report asks for the same measurement or confirmation as the correct ones; the verdict is the only difference. The scorer's VERIFIED gate counts a finding as supported when its quotation is on the cited line, so these are not unsupported VERIFIED findings in the preregistered sense: the line does state the admission. They are overclaims in the corpus's sense (the correct verdict is GO_WITH_CHANGES).
findings.defectTwins: No defect twin lacked NO_GO; none was read beyond its machine summary or verdict line. The skill-style reports carry one VERIFIED BLOCKER on the decisive line (checked by the scorer) in each of the 32 observations.

limits: A reading by the corpus author after the scores. The 26 correct gap twins, ten hedged sound plans, the single GO and nine overclaims were read; the other reports were read only through their verdicts, findings and the keyword rubric. The keyword rubric (recall only) found the gap named in 27 of 32 skill-style, 27 of 32 defined and 29 of 32 defined-go twins, so its misses (five, five and three) are not confirmed absences: every report I read named the gap in words the rubric does not list, and the rubric was not tuned afterwards. In every evidence-gap family the plan states the unknown in one explicit sentence, so these results show what a reviewer does with a stated unknown, not whether it finds an unstated one.
